newsitem.title: UK: EU hits British hopes of easing beef ban - BBC.
newsitem.headline: EU hits British hopes of easing beef ban - BBC.

text.p: The European Union's executive commission has cast serious doubt on British proposals to relax a damaging ban on beef exports imposed last year because of fears about mad cow disease, the BBC said on Friday.

The news is yet another blow for the ruling Conservative government, widely blamed for mishandling the crisis over bovine spongiform encephalitis (BSE), and looks set to maintain tensions with the EU before Britain's May 1 election.

Britain, urgently trying to persuade the EU to ease the economically and politically damaging ban, proposed in February to set up a "certified herd scheme" to identify cows from BSE-free herds which could then be exported.
But the BBC said it had received a copy of a letter which two commissioners had written to Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg expressing doubts about the scheme.
Agriculture commissioner Franz Fischler and consumer affairs commissioner Emma Bonino questioned whether farmers' records could be trusted to prove that certain herds were BSE-free.
They also said a new central computerised system to keep track of healthy cows had been set up too recently to be of any use at this stage.

The ban is one of the most serious sources of tension between Britain's European partners and the government of John Major, which last year infuriated the EU by blocking all the 15-nation bloc's business in protest.
The opposition Labour Party, which has a commanding opinion poll lead over the ruling Conservatives, has consistently criticised the government over the BSE crisis.
On Tuesday, Major called for an end to the ban and dropped a hint he would sack Hogg if he won the May 1 election.
Fischler and Bonino wrote an earlier joint letter to the British government only last week saying the request to ease the ban was being considered.
The letter leaked to the BBC seemed to indicate that a group of European Union scientists, asked to report by the end of May on the British proposal, could well reject it.
Beef exports from Britain were banned by the EU in March last year after the brain-wasting mad cow disease was linked to the human equivalent Creutzfeld-Jakob disease (CJD).

European Commission spokesmen have ruled out any early easing of the ban, saying more veterinary inspections were needed to check whether Britain had complied fully with last year's Florence agreement which provided a framework under which the ban might eventually be lifted.
